The Slavs 'mostly settled the western half of the peninsula'; the Macedonian Sclaviniae are placed by the sieges of Thessalonica (614-617, 676-678). ledger.note: 586: the Slavs overrun Greece. 'Slavs raided the western Peloponnese, Attica, and Epirus' in 586 and a raid on Thessalonica of up to 100,000 Slav warriors is reported; John of Ephesus wrote in 581 that the Slavs 'plundered all of Greece' (Curta thinks this exaggerated). The Theme of the Peloponnese page: 'From the 580s on' the invasions reached the peninsula, with upheaval peaking around 587 and again under Heraclius (610-641). The region is the researcher's reading: neither page gives a boundary.

region.text: the Macedonian hinterland of Thessalonica, where the Drougoubitai, Sagoudatai, Belegezitai, Baiounetai, Berzetai, Rhynchinoi and Strymonitai besieged the city; Thessalonica itself stayed Byzantine

ledger.note: 783: Staurakios quells the Slavs of Macedonia. 'A large Slavic uprising from Macedonia to the Peloponnese was quelled by Staurakios' in 783 after his campaign of 782-784 from Thessalonica into Thessaly and the Peloponnese, 'transferring many captured Slavs, mostly to Anatolia'. Earlier submissions (Constans II conquered Sklavinia in 657-658) were tribute, not rule.

region.text: the western half of the Peloponnese: 'Slavs mostly settled the western half of the peninsula, while Byzantine authority survived in the eastern mountains and on coastal outposts'

ledger.note: 805: Patras is recovered and the Peloponnese becomes a theme. 'Nikephoros I's governor of Corinth fought the Slavs, and Patras was recovered and resettled with Greeks' (Sclaviniae page, 805); the Theme page: a Slavic siege of Patras failed in 805 or 807 and the theme was created 'in about 800' with Corinth as capital. The Ezeritai and Melingoi remain tribute-paying and autonomous.

ledger.note: 805: the Peloponnesian Sclaviniae end as free Slavic lands, under the new Theme of the Peloponnese (Sclaviniae page: 'Theme of the Peloponnese created' in 805). The mountain tribes of the Ezeritai and Melingoi remain 'relatively autonomous'.

wars.name: Slavic sieges of Thessalonica

zones.text: the Macedonian hinterland of Thessalonica, where the Drougoubitai, Sagoudatai, Belegezitai, Baiounetai, Berzetai, Rhynchinoi and Strymonitai besieged the city; Thessalonica itself stayed Byzantine

wars.outcome: The Drougoubitai, Sagoudatai, Belegezitai, Baiounetai and Berzetai besieged Thessalonica in 614-616; a combined Avar and Slav siege failed in 617; the Rhynchinoi, Sagoudatai, Drougoubitai and Strymonitai besieged it for two years in 676-678 while the Belegezites supplied the city with grain. Thessalonica held.
wars.note: The page calls the 614-616 siege of local significance.

wars.name: Constans II's campaign against the Sclaviniae
wars.outcome: Constans II 'conquered Sklavinia' in 657-658, 'capturing many and subduing', and settled captured Slavs in Asia Minor.

wars.name: Slavic siege of Patras
wars.outcome: A Slavic siege of Patras failed in 805 (or 807); Patras was recovered and resettled with Greeks and the Theme of the Peloponnese was created.
wars.note: The Theme page gives 805 or 807; the Chronicle of Monemvasia reports Skleros's victories in 805.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions); eu-06-x's scope also names 'the Slavic settlement of the Balkans', so a duplicate or overlap may exist outside Greece. Cliopatria has no row. Slug 'sclaviniae-of-greece' (the Wikipedia article 'Sclaviniae' covers the whole Balkans). Two pages opened. These are tribal territories, not a state; type 'state' is a placeholder and the rendering agents may prefer a neutral 'nobody' tint (rule 8) for these lands. Not settled: (1) all boundaries and the dates of tribal control: the pages give raids, sieges and campaigns, not borders (certainty is soft throughout); (2) the Slavs' Thessaly and Epirus (Belegezites in Thessaly is a common reading the page does not state); (3) the Bulgar subjugation of the Macedonian Slavs after 680-681 (page: 'likely', Slavs 'retaining their chiefs in return for tribute and troops'), which is a first-bulgarian-empire matter (eu-18); (4) the Ezeritai and Melingoi of Taygetos (autonomous and tribute-paying, rebellions 840/42 and 921/22; Constantine VII's 'Slavonized' Peloponnese after the 744-747 plague) persist after 805 and are not drawn; (5) Willibald's 732 Monemvasia 'in the land of Slavinia'; (6) capitals: none (tribal).
